newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile, Evergreen sign oil exploration deal.
newsitem.headline: Chile, Evergreen sign oil exploration deal.

text.p: Chile's state oil company Empresa Nacional de Petroleo (Enap) and U.S. energy firm Evergreen Resources signed agreements to explore for oil and natural gas in two areas in the northern Atacama Desert.
The companies will invest $6 million over the next six years in prospecting and drilling wells in the Tamarugal region which lies north of Iquique, said Evergreen CEO Mark Sexton.
"It is potentially a world class deposit based on the geology. But is high risk," he told reporters at a ceremony to sign the pact.
Early surveys have shown that the area could hold reserves of up to several hundred million barrels of oil, he said.
Denver-based Evergreen owns 75 percent of the joint venture, with the rest held by Enap.
The contract will last for 35 years. The companies plan to carry out exploration in the first 10 years with the project moving into production for the remaining 25 years.
